examples.title: Formatted Markdown
examples.description: Rendered synchronously on first mount, so `data-state` is `rendered` at once and dollar amounts stay literal.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Markdown } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const content = `## Release notes\n\nThe **nightly digest** now runs at _6 a.m._\n\n- Faster delivery\n- Fewer retries`;
</script>

<Markdown {content} />

examples.title: Equations
examples.description: With `math`, the math renderer loads after first paint and `$$…$$` renders as KaTeX; the raw text shows, with its line breaks, until it lands.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Markdown } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const content = `The area is:\n\n$$a = \\pi r^2$$`;
</script>

<Markdown {content} math />

examples.title: Untrusted content
examples.description: With `images` and `links` off, each image renders as its alt text and each link as its text, so the content loads and navigates nothing.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { Markdown } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const content = `See [the docs](https://example.com) and ![a chart](https://example.com/chart.png).`;
</script>

<Markdown {content} images={false} links={false} />
